**Derivation.** Write the Duhamel formulation
$$u(t)=U(t)u_0-\int_0^t U(t-\tau)\,(1-\partial_x^2)^{-1}\partial_x\,(u^p)(\tau)\,d\tau,\qquad U(t)=e^{-t(1-\partial_x^2)^{-1}\partial_x}.$$
The multiplier $m(\xi)=\frac{i\xi}{1+\xi^2}$ satisfies $|m(\xi)|\lesssim\min(|\xi|,|\xi|^{-1})$ and $U(t)$ is unitary on $H^s$.

Take initial data spectrally supported in $|\xi|\sim N$: $\widehat u_0=N^{-s-1/2}(\chi_{[N,2N]}+\chi_{[-2N,-N]})$, so $\|u_0\|_{H^s}\sim1$. In the $p$-th Picard iterate, pairing $p/2$ factors from each bump (for even $p$; a variant handles odd $p$) produces a low-frequency component near $\xi=0$ whose Fourier transform has height $h\sim N^{-ps+p/2-1}$ and width $\sim N$. Because the input phases satisfy $\sum m(\xi_j)\approx0$ on this support, the time integral contributes only a factor $t$. Applying the symbol $m(\xi)$ and taking the $H^s$ norm (dominated by the low-frequency region when $s<1/2$) gives a lower bound
$$\big\|\text{$p$-th iterate}(t)\big\|_{H^s}\gtrsim t\,N^{-ps+p/2-1}.$$
Boundedness as $N\to\infty$ requires $-ps+p/2-1\le0$, i.e. $s\ge\frac12-\frac1p$. Below this exponent the $p$-linear term is unbounded, so the flow map cannot be $C^p$. Above it, standard fractional Leibniz rules combined with the smoothing of $(1-\partial_x^2)^{-1}\partial_x$ close a contraction argument in $C([0,T];H^s)$, giving unconditional local well-posedness. Hence the sharp threshold is $s_c(p)=\frac12-\frac1p$.
